entries.title: How do orchestra musicians play together?
entries.answer: An orchestra is a group of musicians who play different instruments together. A typical orchestra includes strings, woodwinds, brass, and percussion. The groups may play different parts at the same time. To line up their sounds, musicians follow written music and listen to each other. Many orchestras have a conductor who uses gestures to show when to start, how fast to play, or when to get quieter. The same group can make a tiny sound or fill a large room with music.
facts: Violins and cellos belong to the string family.
Trumpets belong to the brass family.

entries.title: How do written notes tell us what to play?
entries.answer: Written music gives performers a set of marks to follow. In a familiar kind of musical notation, notes sit on or between five lines called a staff. Moving a note higher on the staff usually shows that it should sound higher. The note’s shape can tell how long the player should hold it. A rest marks time when that player should be silent. People can learn and share many kinds of music by ear too. Written music is one way to keep a record that others can follow.
facts: A musical staff has five lines in common Western staff notation.
A rest can show a short silence or a long one.

entries.title: Is rhythm the same as the beat?
entries.answer: The beat is the steady pulse you can tap along to in much music. Rhythm is the pattern made by sounds and silences as time goes by. Try tapping slowly and evenly with one hand while a partner says “I can run.” Your partner can bunch the syllables together or stretch them across more than one tap. In an orchestra or a band, one person can play quick sounds while another plays slow ones, and both can still fit into the same beat.
facts: A pause can be part of a rhythm.
A rhythm can put several short sounds in the time of one beat.
